skill.name: react
skill.description: React renderer for json-render that turns JSON specs into React components. Use when working with @json-render/react, building React UIs from JSON, creating component catalogs, or rendering AI-generated specs.
skill.summary: Guidance for rendering JSON UI specs with typed React catalogs, registries, state, events, and bindings.
skill.author: vercel-labs

content.user_title: Build React UIs from JSON Specs
content.value_statement: Static React interfaces are difficult to generate and maintain from structured data. This skill explains how to render JSON specs, define catalogs, manage state, and connect events in React.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to render JSON element trees with the React Renderer and a component registry.
Shows how to define catalogs with typed props, slots, descriptions, and validation schemas.
Documents state providers, external stores, visibility conditions, dynamic expressions, and two-way bindings.
Explains event emission, event handles, watchers, built-in state actions, and form validation.
Lists the main exports and demonstrates reusable components with BaseComponentProps and useBoundProp.
limitations: It documents the @json-render/react API but does not install packages or run a React project.
It does not design a complete application, backend, authentication flow, or production deployment.
The examples depend on the current json-render package APIs and may require updates after version changes.
Security, authorization, and validation for application-specific actions remain the integrator's responsibility.

use_cases.title: Prototype JSON-driven screens
use_cases.description: Create a small React renderer and catalog for an interface whose layout and content arrive as structured JSON.

use_cases.title: Connect forms to application state
use_cases.description: Use state bindings, validation, watchers, and built-in actions to build interactive forms from JSON specs.

use_cases.title: Build reusable component libraries
use_cases.description: Define typed registries and catalog-agnostic components that can render shared JSON UI patterns across projects.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the quick start
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the smallest setup for rendering a JSON spec with @json-render/react. Identify each import and explain the registry relationship.

prompt_templates.title: Create a typed catalog
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a catalog with a Button and Card component. Include typed props, a default slot, descriptions, and matching type-safe registry implementations.

prompt_templates.title: Add bound form state
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to build a form input that reads and writes a state path with useBoundProp. Explain the bindings map and validation result handling.

prompt_templates.title: Architect an interactive renderer
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a JSON-driven React screen with external state, conditional visibility, named slots, event actions, watchers, and reusable catalog-agnostic components. Identify integration risks.

output_examples.input: How do I render a JSON card containing a button?
output_examples.output: Define a catalog and registry, then pass the JSON element tree and registry to Renderer. The card receives its typed title prop and renders its child button.

output_examples.input: How can an input update shared state?
output: Bind the input value to a state path with the documented binding expression.
Use useBoundProp inside the component to read the resolved value and write changes back through the provided binding.

output_examples.input: Which exports support an interactive application?
output_examples.output: Use Renderer and defineRegistry for rendering, StateProvider or createStateStore for state, useBoundProp for two-way form binding, and useAction or useActions for event actions.

best_practices: Define typed prop schemas and keep catalog descriptions aligned with the component behavior.
Use natural value properties with documented binding expressions for two-way form state.
Keep application-specific actions, authorization, and external state policies explicit at the integration boundary.
anti_patterns: Do not use slots.default for named content; use children for the default slot and the top-level slots object for named slots.
Do not add a statePath prop for two-way binding when the documented binding expression and useBoundProp flow are required.
Do not treat generated JSON specs or action names as trusted application policy without validation and authorization.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It explains how to use @json-render/react to turn JSON element trees into React components through catalogs and registries.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete React application?
faq.answer: No. It provides focused API guidance and examples, while application architecture and implementation remain your responsibility.

faq.question: How are named slots represented?
faq.answer: Use children for the default slot and the element's top-level slots object for named regions declared by the catalog.

faq.question: How does two-way binding work?
faq.answer: Use the documented binding expression on a natural value prop, then use useBoundProp with the renderer-provided bindings map.

faq.question: Can it use external state management?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented StateStore interface can connect StateProvider or createRenderer to systems such as Redux, Zustand, or XState.

faq.question: What should I secure when using generated specs?
faq.answer: Validate specs, restrict registered actions, and enforce authorization before allowing state changes or application-specific side effects.
